Subject: Quick help: compatibility gaps between LangBridge SDK and Redwood runtime

Hi Monica —

Thanks for taking a look at this. PromptFlow Labs is building an official LangBridge adapter and an IndexLink connector (for IndexLink-based retrieval) to make Redwood a first-class target in our ISV integrations gallery. During early runs against your hosted endpoint we found a few reproducible interop gaps that block streaming+trace metadata and make our SDK error handling brittle. I attached a short gap matrix and a diff from our SDK integration test.

Topline issues:
- Streaming payloads sometimes split the trace headers (trace-id / parent-id) between prefix flushes.
- KV cache behavior differs when the tokenization boundary is in the middle of a prompt placeholder.
- Error codes for model-fallback are not machine-parsable in the same way our LangBridge adapter expects (we rely on a structured code + reason).

We'd love to run an engineering triage with someone from runtime and a partner-program contact next week. Proposed attachments: interop-gap-matrix.xlsx, sdk-compatibility-diff.txt.

Are you available for a 45m call on Mon/Tue (PST)? If useful I can loop Ravi (IndexLink) — he has the retrieval-side reproducible test cases.

Thanks,
Evelyn Grant
Head of Integrations, PromptFlow Labs

On Sun, Nov 29, 2026 at 11:03 AM Monica Patel wrote:
> Really appreciate the detailed matrix and the test diff.

Thanks — I dug into the diff overnight. Short technical notes before the call:

1) Streaming / trace headers: We do stream flushes at token-chunk boundaries. The trace metadata is sent as part of the first chunk; older SDKs assume the headers arrive in the same frame as the first token. We can add an explicit trace-framing flag (X-Redwood-Trace-Start) that preserves headers on every chunk or include a small preface frame.

2) KV tokenization edge-case: The tokenizer we use for quantized models normalizes certain placeholder characters. When a placeholder straddles the tokenizer boundary our prefix cache store uses the normalized tokens, so subsequent lookups miss. Short-term: we'll add a canonicalize step when storing/retrieving cache keys. Long-term: align tokenizer configs in the SDK.

3) Error codes/fallbacks: Agree the payload is too freeform. We can introduce a structured error envelope with {code, reason, fallback_model} so the LangBridge adapter can make deterministic decisions. We'll try a backwards-compatible envelope for the v1.1 patch.

For the call I will bring a small reproducibility harness and a branch with suggested changes. Monica — can you provision a sandbox token with scope 'isv:interop' for PromptFlow and IndexLink?

-Karthik
